theme.title: Mixed / Stock-Picker's Market
theme.summary: Consumer Staples (+2.58%) and Health Care (+2.00%) led the market today, while Energy (-2.13%) and Industrials (-1.98%) brought up the rear. That split lines up with a rotation out of growth: growth-oriented sectors averaged -1.12% versus +1.97% for defensives and -0.39% for value and cyclicals, suggesting money moved from high-multiple names into steadier, cash-generative businesses. That shows up at the index level too: the blue-chip Dow gained +0.11% while the tech-heavy Nasdaq fell -2.08%, a wide enough gap to matter. Small caps bucked the broader trend, with the Russell 2000 up -0.06%, outperforming large caps. The VIX rose 9.95% to 18.34, pointing to a bit more caution creeping in beneath the surface. Gold slipped 1.17% to $4,059.10, crude oil was little changed at $98.77, and bitcoin slipped 3.04% — cross-asset moves weren't all pointing the same direction as equities.
